citations.quote: ### domain layer
This is the "domain" or "entities" layer. Here's the description by Uncle Bob:
├── domain - Domain Layer

units.claim: The domain layer resides under src/domain/** and encapsulates domain models and use-case interfaces as the innermost enterprise business rules layer.

citations.quote: ### application layer
This is the **"Use Cases"** layer. Here you may add the application **Use cases**. Here's the description by Uncle Bob:
├── application - Application or Use cases layer

units.claim: The application layer resides under src/application/** and contains concrete use cases, port interfaces (including repository interfaces), validations, and application errors.

citations.quote: ### adapters (presentation) layer
I'm using the name **"Presentation"** for this layer.
└── presentation - Presentation layer

units.claim: The presentation layer resides under src/presentation/** and acts as the interface adapters layer containing concrete controllers, application-specific middlewares, and response classes.

citations.quote: ### infrastructure layer
This folder (layer) is where we add everything related to external "**Frameworks and Drivers**". Here you can add the repositories, external frameworks, web and so on.
├── infrastructure - Infrastructure layer

units.claim: The infrastructure layer resides under src/infrastructure/** and houses external frameworks and drivers including Express web setup and routes, Knex database configuration, and SQL repository implementations.

citations.quote: ### main layer
This layer is where we put everything together. It's the "dirty layer", because most factories will be here. It may depend on all other layers in the system.
├── main - Main layer

units.claim: The main layer resides under src/main/** and serves as the composition root containing controller and middleware factories that wire the other layers together.

citations.quote: There's also another layer called "common" that you can use as a [cross-cutting concern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-cutting_concern) layer. In this layer, you may add things that can be used in all other layers, as validations and helpers.
This layer is where we put everything together. It's the "dirty layer", because most factories will be here. It may depend on all other layers in the system.

>The overriding rule that makes this architecture work is The Dependency Rule. This rule says that source code dependencies can only point inwards. Nothing in an inner circle can know anything at all about something in an outer circle. In particular, the name of something declared in an outer circle must not be mentioned by the code in the an inner circle. That includes, functions, classes. variables, or any other named software entity.

In our case, data enter the system via "express routes" (infrastructure layer) to the "controllers" (adapters layer), to the "use cases" (application layer), to the "domain" (domain/entities layer). Then the system outputs via "domain" -> "use cases" -> "presentation" -> "infrastructure". I'm using the "main" layer to create factories for "middlewares", and "controllers" (and possibly other factories).

units.claim: The layers are ordered from innermost to outermost as domain, application, presentation, infrastructure, and main, with source dependencies pointing inward and src/common left unlayered as a cross-cutting concern used across all layers.

citations.quote: This is my attempt to create an API with [node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/) and [typescript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/) following the principles of [clean architecture](https://blog.cleancoder.com/uncle-bob/2012/08/13/the-clean-architecture.html). I'm using [express.js](https://expressjs.com/pt-br/), but the idea is that you can replace it with any framework you want.

For data storage, I'm using [knex query builder](http://knexjs.org/), so you can use Postgres, MSSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite3, Oracle, and Amazon Redshift. Again, you can change the data storage with anything you want. You can create new repositories in `src/infrastructure/repositories`. You can add NoSQL too if needed, but you'll have to create your own repository (I might create an example in the future).

units.claim: FF-P01 (domain-purity) adds knex to forbidden_imports alongside express and the preset's ORMs because the repository uses the Knex query builder for persistence in the infrastructure layer.
